validity.recommendation: Operator cell names only the Belarus operator. Add the Ukrainian gas transmission operator for the Ukrainian section. Treat 22 bcm/y as a nominal figure: the pipe has no compressor stations and has carried 1.5 to 2.7 bcm a year.
validity.researcher_notes: The line is real and separate from the Ivatsevichy-Dolyna pair. The iSANS report (2023) lists Torzhok-Dolina 1420 mm, about 22 bcm a year, apart from the twin Ivatsevichy-Dolina line at 1220 mm. The Gazprom Transgaz Belarus page lists both as separate trunks. Ukrainian Wikipedia says it was built from 1989, finished as pipe by 1995 to 1996 with 529 km in Ukraine, and never got its compressor stations. So the 22 bcm/y is a nominal figure and the real use was low. The sheet lists the operator as the Belarus company only, though the line ends in Ukraine. The 1,300 km total length could not be confirmed.

fills.researcher_notes: A February 2023 report by the iSANS research group on Belarus energy security gives about 22 billion cubic meters a year for the Torzhok-Dolina line, 1420 mm. This matches the sheet. One source only. The link is already on the sheet and it does name the line.
Two separate publishers agree on 1420 mm for the Torzhok-Dolina line: the iSANS report (2023) and the activities page of Gazprom Transgaz Belarus (2023 web archive capture). Both name the line.

The cited Cyberleninka article is a page that needs a browser to load, so it could not be read here. It was not checked and stays on the sheet. No other source found for a total length of 1,300 km. Ukrainian Wikipedia says only that 529 km of the line lie in Ukraine. A 2011 Ukrainian paper found in search gives 206 km for one Ukrainian section. Searched in Russian and Ukrainian.

fills.researcher_notes: Ukrainian Wikipedia says the pipe itself was finished in 1995 to 1996, including 529 km in Ukraine. The Ukrainian operator's history table for 1995 lists 57.6 km of Torzhok-Dolina second stage. Caveat: there were no compressor stations, so the line carried far less than its design. The 2007 flow was only 1.5 to 2.7 billion cubic meters.

verifications.note: line listed as a current Belarus transit trunk in 2023

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The newest dated evidence is from 2023 and covers the Belarus section only. No source dated 2024 or later was found saying the Ukrainian section is in use or idle. The line was never a main transit route and ran well under design. Status stays operating, with low certainty about use after the end of Russian transit on 2025-01-01. Absence of news is not a reason to change it.

cross_row_leads.facts: iSANS 2023 calls Ivatsevichy-Dolina a two-thread line, 1220 mm, about 30 bcm a year for the whole system (not per string).

summary: "Real, separate from P3484/P5938; attribution caveat on operator; length 1300 km and Owner unresolved; 22 bcm/y nominal"
